correctness.rationale: From the exact logarithmic fitness replicator, u=log((1-x)/x),v=log((1-y)/y) obey u_dot=alpha log(1+e^v)+alpha0 log(1+e^-v) and v_dot=beta log(1+e^u)+beta0 log(1+e^-u). Both derivatives have positive global minima and at-most-linear growth, so interior global solutions have u,v→+infty. For sufficiently large time, u_dot=alpha v+rA(v), v_dot=beta u+rB(u) with rA,rB positive bounded and →0. W=√beta u+√alpha v, Z=√beta u-√alpha v yield W_dot=√(alpha beta)W+F, Z_dot=-√(alpha beta)Z+G. Variation of constants gives finite L>0 and W-Le^(lambda t)→0, Z→0 (not merely little-o of e^lambda t), proving the stronger multiplicative asymptotics and ratio. Independent bounded log-odds ODE integrations agree; no finite integration proves t→infty.
